1: Welcome ceremony, afternoon stroll through Paro's farmhouses and old market.
Full-day ascent to Paro Taktsang (3,120m). Packed lunch at the cliff café.
Tashichho Dzong, Buddha Dordenma, Folk Heritage Museum, traditional archery.
108 memorial chortens in morning mist; breathtaking Himalayan panorama.
Most beautiful dzong at the confluence of two rivers, built in 1637.
Remote valley opened to tourists in 2002. Visit Lhakhang Karpo and Nagpo.
Handicraft shopping, red rice wine, authentic ema datshi with a local family.
Morning meditation walk, airport transfer with blessing scarves (khata).
2: Arrival & Festival Briefing
Welcome dinner with our cultural expert. Festival etiquette orientation.
Pre-Festival Village Walks
Explore Paro town as locals prepare traditional costumes and offerings.
Tsechu Day 1 — Opening Ceremonies
Front-row viewing of opening mask dances, hosted by the Royal Court.
Tsechu Day 2 — Cham Dances
Black Hat Drubchen and deer dance. Backstage access to meet performers.
Tsechu Day 3 — Thongdrel Unveiling
Pre-dawn gathering for the sacred unfurling of the giant appliqué thangka.
Punakha Post-Festival
Drive through Dochula Pass — 108 chortens in lingering festival spirit.
Punakha Dzong & Chimi Lhakhang
Fertility temple of the Divine Madman Drukpa Kunley.
Bumthang Journey
Drive east to Bhutan's spiritual heartland. Jakar Dzong and Jambay Lhakhang.
Bumthang Valley Hikes
Kurjey Lhakhang, apple orchards, traditional black-weaving workshops.
Return to Paro & Departure
Mountain flight, blessing ceremony, farewell gifts.

Altitude acclimatisation and spiritual preparation for the trek.
First ascent through pine forests. Camp with views of Jomolhari.
Highland plateau, first high-altitude lake, wild yak sightings.
Three sacred lakes used by monks for ritual meditation.
Ancient hermitage clinging to the hillside above Thimphu.
Final forest descent into the world's only capital without traffic lights.
Buddha Dordenma, medicine institute, contemporary art gallery.
River picnic at the dzong after trail days.
Traditional hot stone bath, Sowa Rigpa treatments.

Phones stored. Receive traditional gho/kira. Evening breathing exercises.

Traditional Bhutanese medicine assessment and personalised herbal plan.
Tiger's Nest Mindful Pilgrimage
Slow, contemplative ascent. Sit in silence. No schedule, no rush.
Punakha — Riverside Meditation
Dawn yoga at Mo Chhu river, Tibetan singing bowl therapy.
Bumthang Silent Retreat Day 1
Farmhouse retreat. First of two silent days.
Bumthang Silent Retreat Day 2
Forest bathing, nature walks in silence, journalling.

Traditional bath heated with fire-blessed river stones. Deeply healing.
Paro Valley Reintegration
Share your experience with our guide. Final thangka painting class.
Departure with Intention
Personalised wellness prescription and Bhutanese herbal remedies.

4am departure — mist rising over the monastery in first light.
Farmers, children, monks in morning documentary light.
Dzongs, chortens, the giant bronze Buddha.
Fishermen, monks, dzong at dusk reflections.
Yak herders, ancient temples, unchanged village life.
Black-necked cranes at dawn, golden hour panoramas.
Eight centuries of sacred art photographed.
Embedded with a local family — intimate photographic essay.
Lightroom session editing your best shots.

Private Punakha Dzong Sunset
After-hours candlelit dinner in the dzong courtyard.
Spa Day at Amankora
Couples' Sowa Rigpa treatments, hot stone bath, herbal massage.
Phobjikha Romantic Picnic
Champagne and locally sourced mountain fare.
Haa Valley Escape
Remote and rarely visited — your private Himalayan love story.
Bumthang Heritage Night
Private dinner with butter lamp ceremony and folk music.
Thimphu Art & Culture

7: Arrive in Paro
Settle into the valley and meet your local guide for a practical briefing on altitude, roads and cultural etiquette.
Paro’s Sacred Sites
Visit Kyichu Lhakhang and explore Paro’s traditional streets before an easy acclimatisation walk.
Dochula to Punakha
Cross Dochula Pass, with its 108 chortens, and descend toward the warmer Punakha Valley.
Punakha and Chimi Lhakhang
See Punakha Dzong at the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers, then walk through rice fields to Chimi Lhakhang.
Over the Pele La to Trongsa
Travel east through changing forest and mountain scenery; visit the commanding Trongsa Dzong if timing allows.
Into Bumthang
Cross Yotong La and arrive in Bumthang, Bhutan’s cultural heartland, with time for a gentle village walk.
Jakar, Jambay and Kurjey
Explore Jakar Dzong, Jambay Lhakhang and Kurjey Lhakhang with context from your Bhutanese guide.
Tang Valley Stories
Spend the day in the quieter Tang Valley, visiting farms, heritage sites and small craft workshops where available.
Ura Village and Mountain Roads
Follow the high valley road to Ura, known for its distinctive stone houses and open pastoral landscape.
Return Transfer or Departure
Continue by road or domestic connection according to the final transport plan, with timings kept deliberately flexible.
8: Ease into Bhutan with a short walk through the valley and a guide-led introduction to local customs.
Visit Kyichu Lhakhang, the National Museum area and Paro town’s traditional shopfronts.
Drive over Chele La, one of Bhutan’s highest road passes, to the compact and peaceful Haa Valley.
Haa Valley Temples and Village Life
Visit Lhakhang Karpo and Lhakhang Nagpo, then spend time with a local host where arrangements are possible.
Travel back through mountain forest and enjoy a relaxed farmhouse meal or cooking session in the Paro Valley.
Choose a gentle viewpoint walk or a morning at leisure before airport transfer.
9: Arrive in Paro
Meet the trekking team and rest after arrival; hydration and a slow first day set the tone.
Paro Acclimatisation Walk
A guided walk, gear check and discussion of the trek’s elevation profile and leave-no-trace approach.
Drive to Shana and Begin
Travel up the Paro Valley and start walking through blue pine forest beside the river.
Trail to Thangthangka
Follow the valley gradually upward; camp routines and pacing are introduced by the support team.
Arrive at Jangothang
Reach the high camp beneath Jomolhari after a steady ascent through yak pasture and alpine terrain.
Acclimatisation Day
Take an optional short hike or rest day at Jangothang, allowing the group to adapt before higher passes.
Cross toward Lingshi
Trek over a high pass when conditions allow, then descend into a broad valley of stone houses and pasture.
Lingshi to Shodu
Continue through remote mountain country with a route selected for the group’s condition and the weather.
Shodu to Barshong
Walk through forested sections and camp near the remnants of an old dzong site.
Forest Descent
Descend gradually through rhododendron and conifer forest toward the roadhead.
Return to Thimphu
Rejoin the road, travel to Thimphu and enjoy a restorative hot-stone bath if desired.
Thimphu Culture Day
A relaxed capital day with time for handicrafts, the Buddha Dordenma area or quiet café stops.
Paro Departure
Transfer to Paro for departure, with an extra buffer night added when flight schedules or weather call for it.
10: Settle in, meet your guide and review festival etiquette, photography boundaries and the final event programme.
Travel to the capital with stops at traditional bridges, chortens and a local lunch en route.
Visit craft studios and, where open, the National Institute for Zorig Chusum to understand Bhutan’s thirteen traditional arts.
Attend the day’s public ceremonies and masked dances, with context from your guide on the stories and symbols being performed.
Return for a different programme of dances and time to explore the market atmosphere around the event.
Leave the capital for the 108 chortens at Dochula and continue into the river valleys of Punakha.
Visit the dzong from its riverside approach before returning to Paro for a final evening.
Airport transfer or an optional extra day in Paro, depending on the confirmed festival and flight schedule.
11: Settle into Paro with a calm first evening and a simple orientation to the week ahead.
Choose a gentle riverside or hillside walk, with time to visit a temple or simply pause over tea.
Travel over Dochula and settle near Punakha; the afternoon is intentionally left open for rest.
Learn the basics of a Bhutanese meal with a local host and walk through nearby fields at an unhurried pace.
Follow the road to the broad glacial valley of Phobjikha, a place known for quiet trails and open views.
Walk a suitable section of the Gangtey Nature Trail, then take time for reading, journalling or a local hot-stone bath.
Travel back through the mountains, stopping only when the group feels like it — the point is to leave white space.
A final breakfast and airport transfer, or extend with extra nights if a slower return feels right.
12: Meet your guide and prepare for a gentle first day in the valley.
Cross Dochula and visit Punakha Dzong, set where the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu meet.
Drive to the broad glacial valley and visit the crane information centre when it is open.
Observe black-necked cranes from designated areas during their season, then walk a gentle section of the Gangtey Nature Trail.
Explore Gangtey village and monastery surroundings, with a locally paced visit to farms or craft makers where possible.
Travel west through the mountains, pausing for landscapes, tea and road-side chortens.
Choose a Tiger’s Nest viewpoint walk, a full hike if suitable, or head directly to the airport.

Designed for a quiet pace. Meditation, traditional wellness treatments and hot-stone baths are arranged around local availability rather than a rigid daily timetable.
5: A small group format leaves room for changing light and local events. Respectful photography guidance is included for monasteries, people and festival settings.
6: Mar–May · Sep–Nov

7: Mar–May · Sep–Nov

gmc: A new city in the making
A stop on a southern journey

Announced by His Majesty the King in December 2023, Gelephu Mindfulness City is a Special Administrative Region of about 2,500 km² on the border with Assam. It is planned around mindfulness, green energy and well-being, with neighbourhoods linked by forest and river corridors.
Gelephu is a road entry from India and has a domestic airport; pair a visit with the Gelephu hot springs or Royal Manas National Park.
buddha: A monumental Buddha overlooking Thimphu from Kuenselphodrang. Explore the surrounding viewpoint and discover its Buddhist symbolism with a local guide.
Ask your guide about current access before visiting; restoration work may affect entry.
memorial: A white chorten with a golden spire in the heart of Thimphu. Observe daily prayer and circumambulation with your guide.
Walk clockwise and ask before photographing worshippers.
museum: Explore Bhutanese art and cultural heritage at Ta Dzong, the historic watchtower above Rinpung Dzong in Paro.
Check opening times and photography rules with your guide.
taktsang: A monastery clinging to the cliffs above Paro. Take the ascent slowly, pause beneath the prayer flags, and let the valley open up below you.
Allow a dedicated hiking day; the climb is steep in places.
rinpung: White fortress walls, timber galleries and a monastic community in the Paro valley. A rewarding introduction to Bhutan’s dzong architecture.
Explore with a guide and check which courtyards are open.
tashichho: Thimphu’s fortress-monastery brings Bhutan’s monastic and government traditions together. Look closely at the carved details and layered roofs.
Visit times depend on official and religious use.
crafts: Discover the textiles, painting and craftsmanship that shape Bhutanese daily life. This city marker represents Thimphu’s cultural experiences, rather than a single workshop.
Ask your guide to include a weaving or artisan visit.
dochula: A cluster of 108 chortens marks the pass between Thimphu and Punakha. Clear weather opens Himalayan views; forest paths offer a quieter way to linger.
Mountain views depend on cloud and weather.
punakha: Founded in 1637, this landmark combines massive stone walls with richly decorated interiors. It remains an important place of Bhutanese religious and civic life.
Give yourself time for the approach and the courtyards.
chimi: A hilltop temple near Lobesa in the Punakha valley. Combine the visit with a walk through the surrounding settlement and agricultural landscape.
Follow your guide’s advice on local customs.
gangtey: Gangtey’s monastery anchors the spiritual life of the valley. Its courtyards and traditional architecture make a natural companion to a walk through Phobjikha.
Pair the monastery with the nearby nature trail.
phobjikha: A broad glacial valley with farms, pine forests and wetlands. Black-necked cranes winter here, while the Gangtey nature walk offers a gentle introduction to the landscape.
Winter is the crane season; observe from a respectful distance.
trongsa: A vast fortress-monastery overlooking the Mangde Chhu gorge. Its layered courtyards tell stories of the Wangchuck dynasty and the routes across central Bhutan.
Build time into the journey for a guided heritage visit.
jakar: A hilltop dzong above Jakar, a memorable starting point for exploring Bumthang’s temples, rural settlements and sacred landscapes.
Combine the visit with a slower exploration of the valley.
kurjey: A sacred temple complex in Bumthang. Visit with a local guide who can explain the traditions and stories associated with this important place of worship.
Keep voices low and follow photography instructions.
haa: The White Temple is a landmark of Haa’s quieter valley. Make space for local village life as well as the temple visit.
A good companion to a journey over Chele La.
chelela: A high pass or guided hike
A high mountain pass linking the Paro and Haa valleys. Prayer flags, cool air and forest walks give this crossing a character of its own.
Choose walks according to the day’s weather and your comfort at altitude.
drukpath: A highland trek connecting Paro and Thimphu through forests, ridges and alpine lakes. This marker represents the trekking area, not a particular campsite.
Spring and autumn are commonly chosen; confirm trail conditions with your guide.
jangothang: A highland base camp on the Jomolhari trekking journey. Mountain scenery and yak country make this a very different experience from the valley tours.
Plan acclimatisation and a route matched to your trekking experience.
trashigang: Part of a custom eastern tour
An impressive fortress above Trashigang, founded in 1659. Explore a different side of Bhutan by making room for the towns and traditions of the east.
Ask us to create a longer journey with eastern Bhutan included.

aboutMore: Bhutan is not a place you tick off a list. It is a kingdom you are welcomed into — and for more than fifteen years we have made sure that welcome feels personal.
Guided by those who call it home

Your guides are licensed Bhutanese who call these valleys home. They know when the monastery bells ring at dawn, which farmhouse kitchen welcomes guests, and when it is time simply to stop and listen.
No fixed departures and no crowded coaches. Your route, pace and stays are designed around what moves you, from front-row festival days to silent forest retreats.
We are locally owned and staffed, and carbon-neutral since 2018, so what you spend stays in Bhutanese hands and the mountains stay as clear as you found them.
aboutGnh: Bhutan measures its progress by Gross National Happiness rather than by economic growth alone. Its four pillars below shape how the kingdom welcomes visitors — high value, low volume — and they shape every journey we plan: respectful of culture, gentle on the land, and good for the communities you meet.

A soft-paced introduction to western Bhutan, following old valley roads, white temples and everyday farm life between Paro and Haa.
A classic high-Himalayan route below sacred Jomolhari, combining remote camps, yak-herding country and several days to adjust to altitude.
Thimphu Tsechu — Rituals in the Capital
Built around Bhutan’s best-known capital festival, this journey pairs public Tsechu days with Paro, Punakha and a close look at living craft traditions.
A practical reset built from short walks, mountain air, warm local food and slow evenings in Paro, Punakha and Phobjikha.
A seasonal journey into the wide Phobjikha Valley, combining responsible crane observation with Punakha’s river heritage and Paro’s sacred landscape.
heroDescriptions: Quiet valleys. Living traditions. Extraordinary people. Discover Bhutan through journeys shaped by the locals who call it home.
Follow forest trails to cliffside monasteries and open Himalayan horizons. In Bhutan, the journey invites you to pause, look closer, and breathe.
Step into dzong courtyards, discover the artistry of sacred festivals, and meet the craftspeople who keep Bhutan’s heritage alive.
Wander through peaceful valleys, share a farmhouse meal, and leave room for unexpected moments. Discover Bhutan at a pace that feels like your own.
From prayer flags on mountain passes to warm welcomes in village homes, find the moments that turn a Bhutan journey into a lasting memory.
